subject: Retained track references refuse observed shape or native-population replacement
question: Do ordinary-to-stack replacement and same-name ordinary insertion invalidate an old reference before it can write a replacement track?

reverify.command: On a stopped disposable eight-track project, issue original track references and independently insert one ordinary track immediately before the sixth track. Give the new track the same name as the original sixth track, then request rename through the original reference in the same MCP process. Compare the complete independent UI before and after refusal. Re-read the tracks resource, rename the new sixth row through its fresh reference and independently verify the original seventh row is unchanged. Stop the candidate before discarding only the owned unsaved fixture changes. The earlier Folder replacement remains a historical shape-discontinuity case.
reverify.expected: The old reference refuses with stale_target_reference before writing and leaves the complete observed UI unchanged. A fresh reference changes only the independently identified new track. An observed unowned membership change retires prior references even for outside rows; the earlier shape-only implementation's outside-reference success is not the current contract.
reverify.cost: One development-only ordinary-track duplication, one same-name preparation, one stale rename refusal, one fresh-reference rename and manual fixture reset; the stale request must perform no write.

method: Independent native UI observations were compared with serial calls to the actual public MCP commands. The original and repaired executables carried their source commits and were content-sealed. Neither the native driver nor the repair substitutes labels or ordinals for a lost reference. Group creation and cleanup were explicit manual fixture operations, not product grouping or compensation.

canon_not_applicable.reason: This reading concerns transient Accessibility-object reuse, source-reference custody and action readback. It makes no claim about a shipped canonical label, menu translation or keyboard binding.

observations.what: Native-population membership custody refuses the stale reference and preserves fresh-reference usability
observations.reference_issuance: Existing logic://tracks resource, ax_live, readable, complete false; not a matched complete-population issuance

conclusion: The historical shape-only repair refused ordinary-to-stack replacement but still allowed an actual same-name ordinary-insertion wrong-target rename. The later membership repair refuses the measured resource-issued old reference before writing, and a fresh reference correctly renames only the new track. Prior references require reread after an observed unowned membership change, including outside rows. Independent UI comparison confirms the refusal is nonmutating. Manual cleanup is not an owned inverse.
limits: The measured English cases cover ordinary/stack shape discontinuity and a same-name ordinary insertion with changed native membership. Same-count unobserved native-object recycling remains unqualified; this is not a logical UUID provider.
The original same-name failure used complete four-domain issuance; the repaired native case used readable partial logic://tracks issuance. This is not matched complete-population qualification.
The fresh-issuance retirement and late-scope variants have injected runtime evidence, not separate native receipts.
This does not qualify arbitrary ordering, automatic grouping, complete hierarchy, physical Folder destruction, audio-routing preservation or automatic compensation.
